listen.script: Hi Nora, it's Lama. About Thursday's project meeting: I know we agreed on the library at four, but my brother can't drive me until after Maghrib prayer. Could we meet online instead? It would save time anyway, since we only need to finalise the slides. If that doesn't work for you, Saturday morning at the library would be my second choice. Let me know tonight if you can.
listen.q: What does Lama most want to do?
options: Meet at the library on Saturday
Meet at the library on Thursday after Maghrib

listen.script: Good evening, and welcome to today's talk on protecting the coral reefs of the Red Sea. Before we begin, a quick note. The question session at the end will be shorter than advertised, because our speaker has a flight to catch straight afterwards. So if there's something you'd really like to ask, you might want to write it on one of the cards on your seat and hand it in during the break.
listen.q: Why are listeners advised to write their questions on cards?
options: There may not be time to ask every question at the end
The speaker prefers written questions to spoken ones
There will be no question session after the talk

read.passage: When Abdullah's grandfather first suggested that the family spend a weekend camping in the desert without phones, Abdullah assumed it would be the longest two days of his life. He had never gone more than a few hours without checking his messages, and the idea of sitting around a fire with nothing to do seemed unbearable. However, by the second evening, something had changed. His grandfather began telling stories about growing up near Ha'il, about finding his way by the stars and sharing what little food there was with neighbours. Abdullah realised he had never really listened to these stories before; he had always been half-distracted by a screen. On the drive home, he surprised everyone by asking when the next trip would be. He still uses his phone, of course, but he now leaves it in another room during family dinners.

qs.q: How did Abdullah feel about the trip before it started?
options: He expected to find it very boring
He was excited to hear his grandfather's stories
He was worried about getting lost in the desert

qs.q: What does the writer suggest about the effect of the trip?
options: It made Abdullah change some of his habits
It made Abdullah stop using his phone completely
It made Abdullah want to move to Ha'il

aloud: If I'd known the exhibition was going to be so popular, I'd have booked our tickets well in advance.

speak.prompt: Some people say teenagers today spend too much time on their phones and not enough time with their families. To what extent do you agree? Give reasons and examples from your own experience, and suggest what could be done about it.
speak.expect: At B2 (GSE 63-66) the learner can give a clear, developed opinion and sustain it for one to two minutes with relevant reasons and personal examples. They can show both sides of the issue (e.g. 'On the one hand… however…') and propose realistic solutions. They link ideas coherently using a range of connectors (although, whereas, as a result, that's why). Expect a reasonable range of vocabulary on the topic (addicted, distracted, balance, quality time), with some paraphrasing when a word is missing. Grammar should include some complex structures, such as conditionals, 'I wish…', modals of advice and relative clauses, with good control. Errors may occur but rarely cause misunderstanding, and the learner can often self-correct. Speech is fairly fluent with only occasional hesitation while searching for expressions. Pronunciation is clearly intelligible, with generally appropriate word and sentence stress.
